finding: Actual Sentinel-5P viewing and solar geometry arrays were extracted. All 48 matched observations had valid values for all four geometry angles on both dates.
interpretation: The geometry analysis uses extracted satellite-product information rather than approximate geometry values.
limitation: Only the selected 48 matched observations and two acquisition dates are represented.

finding: Geometry variables showed substantial interdependence. VIF values were particularly high for viewing zenith and viewing azimuth.
interpretation: Individual geometry effects cannot be cleanly isolated using a large simultaneous regression model.
limitation: Strong predictor collinearity makes individual regression coefficients unstable and difficult to interpret.

finding: Solar and geographic-plus-solar models performed better than the tested baseline and other reduced models in the initial leave-one-out comparison.
interpretation: Solar geometry was a promising predictive feature for the selected methane comparison.
limitation: The initial validation was not spatially blocked.

finding: The solar geometry model achieved pooled MAE 0.2107 and RMSE 0.2553 on the rank-based target. Geographic-plus-solar achieved the best equal-weight quadrant RMSE of 0.2572.
interpretation: Solar geometry was among the strongest tested predictors under spatially blocked evaluation.
limitation: These are rank-scale metrics, not methane concentration errors in ppb. Four sample-derived quadrants provide limited spatial validation.

finding: Solar geometry was a strong pooled ranking predictor. Cross-fitted calibration worsened MAE for all seven evaluated models. The solar model's performance was not uniformly strongest in every quadrant.
interpretation: Raw predictions were retained, and calibration correction was rejected.
limitation: Rank prediction performance does not directly establish physical methane prediction accuracy.

finding: Spearman correlation with signed CH4 difference was +0.3290 for distance, +0.5473 for viewing zenith, +0.5640 for viewing azimuth, -0.0168 for solar zenith and -0.5897 for solar azimuth.
interpretation: Solar azimuth and viewing geometry were associated with signed methane differences in this sample. Associations with absolute methane differences were much weaker.
limitation: Correlation is not causation. Geometry variables are interdependent, and the sample contains only 48 matched pairs.

finding: The signed associations for distance, viewing zenith, viewing azimuth and solar azimuth retained their directions when individual observations were removed. Solar zenith association was unstable.
interpretation: Several signed associations were not driven by one individual observation.
limitation: Leave-one-out robustness does not establish independent spatial or temporal generalization.

finding: Solar azimuth difference alone achieved LOOCV MAE 7.9635 ppb and RMSE 10.3658 ppb, outperforming the tested reduced predictor combinations.
interpretation: A parsimonious solar-azimuth model was preferred over adding more geometry predictors.
limitation: The model is exploratory and based on 48 matched observations from two dates.

finding: The solar-azimuth model improved RMSE in three of four quadrants. Its leave-one-out fitted slopes were negative for all 48 observation-level folds.
interpretation: The negative fitted relationship was stable to individual observation removal, but predictive benefit varied spatially.
limitation: LOOCV does not test transfer to a completely unseen spatial region.

finding: All four spatial training folds produced negative solar-azimuth slopes. Pooled held-out RMSE was 10.2418 ppb versus 15.7078 ppb for the baseline, a 34.8% improvement.
interpretation: The negative fitted relationship retained its direction across all four spatial training folds. The predictive improvement was not uniform: three of four held-out quadrants improved.
limitation: Only four spatial blocks were available, two with six observations each. Quadrant boundaries were calculated using the complete sample. This is not independent external validation.

finding: There were 48 mutual nearest-neighbour matched pixel pairs. Mean matched-pair methane difference was +0.334 ppb, standard deviation 13.278 ppb and mean absolute difference 10.710 ppb.
interpretation: Matched pixels showed substantial local variation between the two acquisition dates.
limitation: The matched sample is sparse and does not represent an India-wide methane trend.

finding: The south-west quadrant had a mean signed difference of +8.403 ppb, while the north-east quadrant had a mean of -7.458 ppb. Their mean contrast was 15.861 ppb.
interpretation: The selected matched observations showed spatial variation in signed methane differences.
limitation: Small sample sizes, spatial dependence and sample-derived quadrant boundaries prevent broad regional conclusions.
